chunks.subject: AP Statistics
chunks.title: Q6 — Investigative Task (4 points)
chunks.content: AP Statistics FRQ 6 is the Investigative Task, 4 points, extending familiar statistics into a novel situation that requires reasoning beyond the standard procedures. Each lettered part is scored E/P/I and combined into an integer 0–4. Typical tasks: analyze given data with standard tools, then apply or derive a new method/quantity the course did not directly teach, and justify the reasoning. Common failure: stopping at the routine parts and not attempting the novel extension; a new-method attempt without justification; interpretations without context. This question is the most discriminating and often the lowest-scoring.

chunks.subject: AP Statistics
chunks.title: Q6 exemplar — Sample 6A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q6 scored 4/4 — all parts essentially correct, including the novel extension with sound justification and contextual interpretation. Full-credit model for the Investigative Task.

chunks.subject: AP Statistics
chunks.title: Q6 exemplar — Sample 6B, 2/4
chunks.content: Q6 scored 2/4 — earned the routine analysis parts but only partially handled the novel extension (attempted without full justification, or with a reasoning gap). Illustrates the common Investigative-Task ceiling — solid on the familiar, incomplete on the new method.

chunks.subject: AP Statistics
chunks.title: Q6 exemplar — Sample 6C, 1/4
chunks.content: Q6 scored 1/4 — completed only part of the routine analysis and did not attempt (or badly mishandled) the novel extension. Illustrates a response that cannot reason beyond standard procedures.
